:::{#exm-lebesgue-measure}
#### Lengths of some Borel sets

- $\lambda([2, 5]) = 5 - 2 = 3$.
- A single point has length zero: $\lambda(\set{a}) = \lambda([a, a]) = a - a = 0$.
- The integers are the union of the pairwise disjoint single points
  $\set{0}, \set{1}, \set{-1}, \set{2}, \set{-2}, \ldots$
  (@exm-borel-sigma-algebra), so countable additivity gives
  $\lambda(\mathbb{Z}) = 0 + 0 + \cdots = 0$.
- $\lambda([0, \infty)) = \infty$, because $[0, \infty)$ is unbounded.
- Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$ gives the whole interval $[0, 1]$
  the value $\lambda([0, 1]) = 1 - 0 = 1$.

:::
